# R2 record lines

## For `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`

Under **Execution model**, after the line on the code generator lowering every type to a
JVM reference type:

- **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact as of the repair batch of 2026-09-18.** `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` chose the numeral's representation by `BigInteger.bitLength()` against `<= 32` and `<= 64`; `bitLength()` counts no sign bit, so a non-negative numeral of bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was truncated into a signed slot and arrived wrapped negative — `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` both became `-1`, against `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86` (a numeral of digits has the value of its digits in radix ten, with nothing bounding it) and `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370,398-401` (wrapping and saturating have their own operator spellings and "operations on type $\mathbb{Z}$ never need to wrap or saturate"). The bounds are now `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` reads the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps. Where the compiled run contradicted `walk` in silence it now agrees with it: `4294967295` at `ZZ` prints `4294967295` on both paths, and `a = 4294967295; b = 1; println (a + b)` prints `4294967296` on both (ledger row 317, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).
- **A radix numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern, and the compile path was the only place that pretended otherwise.** `literals.tex:104-108` gives a radix numeral the type `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]]` over the value of its digits in radix $r$, so `8000'0000_16` is $2^{31}$ and `A0000000_16` is $2684354560$; the interpreter has always refused such a numeral at a signed type ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32"), and the compile path accepted it only because the wrap turned it into something else. Five sites in the tree relied on that: `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571` (`ZZ32_MIN`, `ZZ64_MIN`), `library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` and `Integer4.fss:46` (`twiceHuge`), and `library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss:114` with its ungated twin `ChooseTest3.fss:125`. The first four are repaired value-for-value; the fifth was not only illegal but was exercising `i = -1257966796` instead of the $\sqrt{2^{63}}$ boundary its own comment names.
- Every numeral in the corpora and the libraries whose value has bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 is enumerated, by value and in every radix, at `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/boundary-numerals.txt`; twelve of the seventeen are in range for their annotated type and were right only by the wrap's accident. A decimal-only grep misses the radix-16 half, which is where four of the five out-of-range sites were, and where the `Integer.test` failures came from.
- The bytecode optimizer's `RemoveLiteralCoercions` substitution (`FIntLiteral.make(I)` plus `coerce_ZZ32` becomes `FZZ32.make(I)`, `RemoveLiteralCoercions.java:33-53`) elides `asZZ32`'s range check, which is sound exactly when the code generator's int branch is the `ZZ32`-representable range: false under `l <= 32`, true under `l <= 31`. The optimizer is dormant — reached only from `ByteCodeOptimizer.main` (`ByteCodeOptimizer.java:130,146`), nothing in `Shell` or the compiler driver calls it, its 226 tests off at `default_repository/configuration:50-51` (`map/dormant-code.md:188`) — so this is a latent soundness fact, not live behaviour.

## For `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`

### Row 317 — amend in place

Row 317 is not renumbered and not moved; its existing text stands, with one correction and
one closing paragraph appended to its last column.

**The correction.** In the sentence beginning "Through a **declared** binding it predates
rung 6 and is reached by the coercion `ZZ64.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ64`", the citation
`CompilerBuiltin.fss:557` is stale: that line is now the comment above `ceilingAverage`, and
the `ZZ64` coercion is at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:562`.

**Append to the row's last column:**

> Four things this row did not say. The `ZZ` half: `ZZ.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:501`) renders the wrapped value, so `a: ZZ = 4294967295` was `-1` in the type the specification defines as all the finite integers (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2a.compiled.before`). The defeated `ZZ32` diagnostic: `asZZ32`'s range check is applied to the already-wrapped value and passes on `-1`, so `a: ZZ32 = 4294967295` silently became `-1` instead of raising "Not in range for ZZ32" (`probes/r2c.compiled.before`). The second specification citation: `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370` and `:398-401` give wrapping and saturating their own operator spellings and say ordinary operations "never need to wrap or saturate". And the coupling: `FIntLiteral.asNN32` (`:79-83`) and `asNN64` (`:85-95`) read the wrapped two's-complement pattern as the right unsigned value, so a repair to the code generator alone makes `asNN64` throw (measured: `probes/junit-codegen-only.out`). **Repaired 2026-09-18** by the repair batch's R2 (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`): the two bounds become `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs and the form rung 7's own `simpleIntLiteralArith.java:30-33` already used; `asNN64` learns to read `largerVal`; and `asNN32`'s range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything including the `BOGUS` sentinel, is made to mean what it says. `p37`, `p37a`, `p39`, `r2a` and `r2e` now give the same answer compiled as under `walk`, and three diagnostics the wrap had defeated are restored (`probes/r2c`, `r2d`, `r2f`). The repair uncovered five sites that relied on the wrap and closed four of them; the fifth is the new row below. What it does **not** settle is which number type an untyped numeral's arithmetic happens at: the branch chooses an overload of `FIntLiteral.make`, never a type, and every numeral still has the one flat static type `Types.INT_LITERAL` (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:467-468`), so that fork is untouched and still open.

### Three new rows, at the next free numbers after 318

**319.** *A numeral outside a bounded integer type is a run-time error on the compile path where the specification makes it a static one.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, implementation gap. `literals.tex:83-86` gives a digits-only numeral the type `NaturalNumeral[[n,10,v]]` carrying its value $v$, and `:104-108` the same for a radix numeral, so `a: ZZ32 = 4294967295` is a static error; the checker instead gives every numeral the one flat type `Types.INT_LITERAL` (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:467-468`) and the compiler world's `trait IntLiteral` has six abstract getters and no static parameter (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:370-376`), so nothing in the static types carries the value a checker could range-check. Probes `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2c.fss`, `r2d.fss`, `r2f.fss`, `r2g.fss`, `r2h.fss`, both ways: each compiles clean and raises `Not in range for ZZ32/NN32/ZZ64` at run time, and each is refused by the interpreter at the point of use. Ours. The fix is a static parameter on `IntLiteral` in the compiler prelude and a range check in the checker's literal case; it is a checker-and-prelude rung and was outside R2's scope. Before R2 these five programs did not raise at all — they truncated in silence — so this row is the improved half of what row 317 repaired, not a regression.

**320.** *`NN32` and `NN64` render their values signed on the compile path.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, implementation gap. `FNN32.toString` is `String.valueOf(val)` over a signed `int` (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN32.java:19-20`) and `FNN64.toString` is `"" + val` over a signed `long` (`FNN64.java:20`), so an unsigned value above the type's signed half prints negative: `n32: NN32 = 4294967295` and `n64: NN64 = 18446744073709551615` both print `-1` (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2b.compiled.before` and `.after`, unchanged by R2). The values themselves are right — `compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2.fss:64,69` assert `n32 = h32u + h32u + one32u` and `n64 = h64u + h64u + one64u` and both pass — so this is rendering only. Ours. The fix is `Integer.toUnsignedString` and `Long.toUnsignedString` in those two classes, plus whatever `NN32.asString` and `NN64.asString` reach in the prelude; the interpreter has no comparable site because it refuses the coercion from a numeral to `NN32`/`NN64` altogether (`probes/r2b.walk.before`). Independent of row 317 and untouched by its repair.

**321.** *`library_tests/ChooseTest3.fss:125` exercises a negative binomial coefficient where it means the algorithm's fast/slow boundary.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, defect in a test. `verifyChoose(3037000500+j, 2)` inside `for j <- seq(-3:3)` coerces the numeral at `ZZ32`, because `j` is a `ZZ32` and `3037000500` is outside `ZZ32`; the comment two lines above at `:122-123` says these are "the points that separate use of the fast `ZZ64` algorithm from the slow, cautious algorithm". Under the code generator's wrap the call was `verifyChoose(-1257966796+j, 2)`, so the boundary the file names was never tested, and both sides of `verifyChoose`'s assertions used the same wrong value, which is why nothing showed. The fix is the one R2 applied to the identical line in `IntegerChoose2.fss:114`: bind the constant at `ZZ64` first, which is the file's own idiom. `ChooseTest3.fss` is named in no `.test` file and `LibraryJUTest.java:36` sweeps `.test` files only, so no gate covers it and no measurement of a repair to it is available; R2 left it rather than edit it unverified. Ours.

## For the handover, `explorations/microgpt-run-c-handover.md`

Appended to the state prose, after the rung 8 sentence:

> Repair R2 of the repair batch, the integer-literal wrap in the code generator, landed in its worktree on 2026-09-18 after the batch's first container died: `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr`'s two bounds become `bitLength() <= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` learns to read the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps while `asNN32`'s vacuous mask-and-compare range check is made to mean what it says, with the new test `compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2` passing and `p37`, `p37a`, `p39`, `r2a` and `r2e` now answering compiled what they answer under `walk` (ledger row 317 repaired and amended, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`). Four such sites are repaired with it — `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571`, where `ZZ32_MIN` and `ZZ64_MIN` become a numeral in range and one subtraction in the spelling of `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:703`, and `library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` and `Integer4.fss:46`, where `twiceHuge` becomes the negative numeral of the same bit pattern and so the same value — all value-preserving, plus `library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss`, which binds `3037000500` at `ZZ64` and thereby tests the boundary its comment names instead of a negative `i`. `Integer.test` is `OK (27 tests)` again. The rung tested the batch's named stop condition and it is not met: the branch in `forIntLiteralExpr` chooses an overload of `FIntLiteral.make`, never a type, so the fork over which number type an untyped numeral's arithmetic happens at is untouched. Three new ledger rows are owed (the static-versus-dynamic range diagnostic, the signed rendering of `NN32`/`NN64`, and the ungated `ChooseTest3.fss:125`) and the ladder has no subset to run, because every file of the ladder corpus holding a boundary numeral already fails at compile with return code 255 (`compile-ladder/results.tsv`).

# R2 record lines

## For `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`

Under **Execution model**, after the line on the code generator lowering every type to a
JVM reference type:

- **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact as of the repair batch of 2026-09-18.** `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` chose the numeral's representation by `BigInteger.bitLength()` against `<= 32` and `<= 64`; `bitLength()` counts no sign bit, so a non-negative numeral of bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was truncated into a signed slot and arrived wrapped negative — `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` both became `-1`, against `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86` (a numeral of digits has the value of its digits in radix ten, with nothing bounding it) and `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370,398-401` (wrapping and saturating have their own operator spellings and "operations on type $\mathbb{Z}$ never need to wrap or saturate"). The bounds are now `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` reads the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps. Where the compiled run contradicted `walk` in silence it now agrees with it: `4294967295` at `ZZ` prints `4294967295` on both paths, and `a = 4294967295; b = 1; println (a + b)` prints `4294967296` on both (ledger row 317, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).
- **A radix numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern, and the compile path was the only place that pretended otherwise.** `literals.tex:104-108` gives a radix numeral the type `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]]` over the value of its digits in radix $r$, so `8000'0000_16` is $2^{31}$ and `A0000000_16` is $2684354560$; the interpreter has always refused such a numeral at a signed type ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32"), and the compile path accepted it only because the wrap turned it into something else. Five sites in the tree relied on that: `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571` (`ZZ32_MIN`, `ZZ64_MIN`), `library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` and `Integer4.fss:46` (`twiceHuge`), and `library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss:114` with its ungated twin `ChooseTest3.fss:125`. The first four are repaired value-for-value; the fifth was not only illegal but was exercising `i = -1257966796` instead of the $\sqrt{2^{63}}$ boundary its own comment names.
- Every numeral in the corpora and the libraries whose value has bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 is enumerated, by value and in every radix, at `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/boundary-numerals.txt`; twelve of the seventeen are in range for their annotated type and were right only by the wrap's accident. A decimal-only grep misses the radix-16 half, which is where four of the five out-of-range sites were, and where the `Integer.test` failures came from.
- The bytecode optimizer's `RemoveLiteralCoercions` substitution (`FIntLiteral.make(I)` plus `coerce_ZZ32` becomes `FZZ32.make(I)`, `RemoveLiteralCoercions.java:33-53`) elides `asZZ32`'s range check, which is sound exactly when the code generator's int branch is the `ZZ32`-representable range: false under `l <= 32`, true under `l <= 31`. The optimizer is dormant — reached only from `ByteCodeOptimizer.main` (`ByteCodeOptimizer.java:130,146`), nothing in `Shell` or the compiler driver calls it, its 226 tests off at `default_repository/configuration:50-51` (`map/dormant-code.md:188`) — so this is a latent soundness fact, not live behaviour.

## For `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`

### Row 317 — amend in place

Row 317 is not renumbered and not moved; its existing text stands, with one correction and
one closing paragraph appended to its last column.

**The correction.** In the sentence beginning "Through a **declared** binding it predates
rung 6 and is reached by the coercion `ZZ64.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ64`", the citation
`CompilerBuiltin.fss:557` is stale: that line is now the comment above `ceilingAverage`, and
the `ZZ64` coercion is at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:562`.

**Append to the row's last column:**

> Four things this row did not say. The `ZZ` half: `ZZ.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:501`) renders the wrapped value, so `a: ZZ = 4294967295` was `-1` in the type the specification defines as all the finite integers (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2a.compiled.before`). The defeated `ZZ32` diagnostic: `asZZ32`'s range check is applied to the already-wrapped value and passes on `-1`, so `a: ZZ32 = 4294967295` silently became `-1` instead of raising "Not in range for ZZ32" (`probes/r2c.compiled.before`). The second specification citation: `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370` and `:398-401` give wrapping and saturating their own operator spellings and say ordinary operations "never need to wrap or saturate". And the coupling: `FIntLiteral.asNN32` (`:79-83`) and `asNN64` (`:85-95`) read the wrapped two's-complement pattern as the right unsigned value, so a repair to the code generator alone makes `asNN64` throw (measured: `probes/junit-codegen-only.out`). **Repaired 2026-09-18** by the repair batch's R2 (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`): the two bounds become `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs and the form rung 7's own `simpleIntLiteralArith.java:30-33` already used; `asNN64` learns to read `largerVal`; and `asNN32`'s range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything including the `BOGUS` sentinel, is made to mean what it says. `p37`, `p37a`, `p39`, `r2a` and `r2e` now give the same answer compiled as under `walk`, and three diagnostics the wrap had defeated are restored (`probes/r2c`, `r2d`, `r2f`). The repair uncovered five sites that relied on the wrap and closed four of them; the fifth is the new row below. What it does **not** settle is which number type an untyped numeral's arithmetic happens at: the branch chooses an overload of `FIntLiteral.make`, never a type, and every numeral still has the one flat static type `Types.INT_LITERAL` (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:467-468`), so that fork is untouched and still open.

### Three new rows, at the next free numbers after 318

**319.** *A numeral outside a bounded integer type is a run-time error on the compile path where the specification makes it a static one.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, implementation gap. `literals.tex:83-86` gives a digits-only numeral the type `NaturalNumeral[[n,10,v]]` carrying its value $v$, and `:104-108` the same for a radix numeral, so `a: ZZ32 = 4294967295` is a static error; the checker instead gives every numeral the one flat type `Types.INT_LITERAL` (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:467-468`) and the compiler world's `trait IntLiteral` has six abstract getters and no static parameter (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:370-376`), so nothing in the static types carries the value a checker could range-check. Probes `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2c.fss`, `r2d.fss`, `r2f.fss`, `r2g.fss`, `r2h.fss`, both ways: each compiles clean and raises `Not in range for ZZ32/NN32/ZZ64` at run time, and each is refused by the interpreter at the point of use. Ours. The fix is a static parameter on `IntLiteral` in the compiler prelude and a range check in the checker's literal case; it is a checker-and-prelude rung and was outside R2's scope. Before R2 these five programs did not raise at all — they truncated in silence — so this row is the improved half of what row 317 repaired, not a regression.

**320.** *`NN32` and `NN64` render their values signed on the compile path.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, implementation gap. `FNN32.toString` is `String.valueOf(val)` over a signed `int` (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN32.java:19-20`) and `FNN64.toString` is `"" + val` over a signed `long` (`FNN64.java:20`), so an unsigned value above the type's signed half prints negative: `n32: NN32 = 4294967295` and `n64: NN64 = 18446744073709551615` both print `-1` (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2b.compiled.before` and `.after`, unchanged by R2). The values themselves are right — `compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2.fss:64,69` assert `n32 = h32u + h32u + one32u` and `n64 = h64u + h64u + one64u` and both pass — so this is rendering only. Ours. The fix is `Integer.toUnsignedString` and `Long.toUnsignedString` in those two classes, plus whatever `NN32.asString` and `NN64.asString` reach in the prelude; the interpreter has no comparable site because it refuses the coercion from a numeral to `NN32`/`NN64` altogether (`probes/r2b.walk.before`). Independent of row 317 and untouched by its repair.

**321.** *`library_tests/ChooseTest3.fss:125` exercises a negative binomial coefficient where it means the algorithm's fast/slow boundary.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, defect in a test. `verifyChoose(3037000500+j, 2)` inside `for j <- seq(-3:3)` coerces the numeral at `ZZ32`, because `j` is a `ZZ32` and `3037000500` is outside `ZZ32`; the comment two lines above at `:122-123` says these are "the points that separate use of the fast `ZZ64` algorithm from the slow, cautious algorithm". Under the code generator's wrap the call was `verifyChoose(-1257966796+j, 2)`, so the boundary the file names was never tested, and both sides of `verifyChoose`'s assertions used the same wrong value, which is why nothing showed. The fix is the one R2 applied to the identical line in `IntegerChoose2.fss:114`: bind the constant at `ZZ64` first, which is the file's own idiom. `ChooseTest3.fss` is named in no `.test` file and `LibraryJUTest.java:36` sweeps `.test` files only, so no gate covers it and no measurement of a repair to it is available; R2 left it rather than edit it unverified. Ours.

## For the handover, `explorations/microgpt-run-c-handover.md`

Appended to the state prose, after the rung 8 sentence:

> Repair R2 of the repair batch, the integer-literal wrap in the code generator, landed in its worktree on 2026-09-18 after the batch's first container died: `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr`'s two bounds become `bitLength() <= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` learns to read the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps while `asNN32`'s vacuous mask-and-compare range check is made to mean what it says, with the new test `compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2` passing and `p37`, `p37a`, `p39`, `r2a` and `r2e` now answering compiled what they answer under `walk` (ledger row 317 repaired and amended, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`). specCitations: Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86 — a numeral containing only digits has type NaturalNumeral[[n,10,v]] where v is the value of the numeral interpreted in radix ten; nothing bounds v. This is what the wrap violated.

Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:104-108 — a radix numeral has type NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]] over the value of its n digits interpreted in radix r. A radix-16 numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern; this clause decides the second half of the rung.

Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370 and :398-401 — the wrapping and saturating operators do exactly the same thing as + and - "because operations on type ZZ never need to wrap or saturate"; wrapping has its own spelling and is not what an ordinary operation or coercion does.

Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-148 — numerals are not directly converted to any number type and Part Library defines coercions from numerals to integers; silent on WHICH number type, which is the reserved fork, tested and not triggered.

The branch was relaunched after the container died: commit 7e666704 held the failing test and probes/junit-before.out, and the worktree held uncommitted edits whose last log line showed Integer.test starting and never finishing. Everything was re-run rather than trusted, including javap on the built classes, and the measurements phase B never reached were taken fresh.

Part one is the repair the brief describes. CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr's bounds become bitLength() <= 31 and <= 63, exact for both signs; FIntLiteral.asNN64 learns to read the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps, which was forced and measured (junit-codegen-only.out); asNN32's range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything, is made to mean what it says, which was a decision and not forced — the brief's premise about asNN32 is corrected in the report.

Part one then turned library_tests/Integer.test from green to four failures, all one thing: a radix numeral whose value is outside the annotated signed type, written to mean a two's-complement bit pattern. literals.tex:104-108 gives such a numeral the value of its digits in its radix, and probes r2g and r2h show the interpreter has always refused the idiom, so these are not correct programs the repair broke — they are programs the language does not accept, on which the two paths now agree. The repair reduces divergence and creates none.

The blast radius was enumerated by value in every radix rather than grepped decimally, which is how the radix-16 half was found. Eighteen lines on the compile path, twelve in range and now right for the right reason, six out of range. Five are repaired: ZZ32_MIN and ZZ64_MIN in the prelude (value-identical, in FortressLibrary.fss:703's spelling), twiceHuge in Integer3 and Integer4 (value-identical, same bit pattern written legally, assertions unchanged), and IntegerChoose2, where 3037000500 is bound at ZZ64 so the test exercises the fast/slow boundary its comment names instead of a negative i. Integer.test is OK (27 tests) again; the rung's own test passes.

The batch's one named stop was tested and is not met: the branch in forIntLiteralExpr chooses an overload of FIntLiteral.make, never a type, every numeral still has the flat static type Types.INT_LITERAL, and r2e and p39 show the arithmetic still happening at IntLiteral — it merely starts from the right operand now. That fork is untouched and still open. Three new ledger rows are owed and named in record.md.

Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:104-108 — a radix numeral has type NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]] over the value of its n digits interpreted in radix r. A radix-16 numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern; this clause decides the second half of the rung.

Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370 and :398-401 — the wrapping and saturating operators do exactly the same thing as + and - "because operations on type ZZ never need to wrap or saturate"; wrapping has its own spelling and is not what an ordinary operation or coercion does.

Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-148 — numerals are not directly converted to any number type and Part Library defines coercions from numerals to integers; silent on WHICH number type, which is the reserved fork, tested and not triggered.

Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:40-45 — coercion converts a value of one type to a value of another; nothing licenses truncation, which is consistent with the prelude's own asZZ32 range check and its outOfRange("ZZ32") error.

r2e and rung 7's p39, literal arithmetic through bindings: walk 4294967296, compiled 0. literals.tex:83-86 with basic-integers.tex:368-370 settles it against the compiled run. Repaired; identical both ways now.

r2c, r2d, r2f, out-of-range coercions: walk refuses, compiled silently truncated (ZZ32 4294967295 to -1, NN32 4294967296 to 0, ZZ64 2^64-1 to -1). r2b, NN32 and NN64 rendering: walk refuses the coercion from a numeral altogether, compiled prints -1 for both 2^32-1 and 2^64-1. Unchanged by this rung. decisions: Repairing the prelude and three corpus files rather than stopping and landing nothing. Rejected alternative: report part one's four red Integer.test failures to Pavol. Rejected because PLAN.md:47 says "any source in the tree may be edited under the rule above; which file it is in is not a decision"; because none of that clause's stops fires (no design fork, the change of semantics is toward the specification not against it, no test deleted, first repair not a second); and because the prelude half is forced anyway — with CompilerLibrary.fss:569 as written, ZZ32_MIN's class initialiser throws and nothing on the compile path touching the number properties runs. This widens the rung past the two files the brief named, which is why it is recorded as a decision.

Value-preserving rewrites of Integer3.fss:46 and Integer4.fss:46 rather than moving the two files to not_working_library_tests/. 0xA0000000 read as a signed 32-bit value is -0x60000000, so -60000000_16 is the same ZZ32 and the assertions it feeds (Integer3.fss:99,106) assert exactly what they asserted. Moving was rejected because a faithful rewrite exists and because those two files are the only tests of the BOXPLUS/BOXMINUS/BOXDOT/DOTPLUS wrapping and saturating operators at ZZ32 and ZZ64.

Repairing FIntLiteral.asNN32 although nothing forced it. Rejected alternative: leave a vacuous range check beside a repaired asNN64. The brief's premise that asNN32 "depends on the wrap" and would "begin throwing" is true of asNN64 (measured) and not of asNN32: masking a long to its low 32 bits always lands in [0, 0xFFFFFFFF], so the old guard accepted every value and could not throw — it truncated, silently turning 2^32 at NN32 into 0 (probes/r2d). Repaired because it is three lines from the comment that asks for this rung.

Three branches in forIntLiteralExpr kept, not collapsed to simpleIntLiteralArith's two. make(int) and make(long) both store a long, so the int branch buys nothing at run time. Kept because the bytecode optimizer matches on it (RemoveLiteralCoercions.java:33-53 rewrites FIntLiteral.make(I) plus coerce_ZZ32 to FZZ32.make(I)), and the repair makes that substitution sound: it elides asZZ32's range check, which is safe exactly when the int branch is the ZZ32 range. Flagged in the report as dormant code, not live behaviour: the optimizer is reached only from ByteCodeOptimizer.main and its 226 tests are off at default_repository/configuration:50-51.

asZZ32 left alone. It is correct for a string-carried numeral only because the BOGUS sentinel 0xdeadbeefcafebabe falls outside int range. Adding largerVal == null would change no behaviour today; left out to keep the diff to what the tests need, with the dependency on the sentinel recorded instead.

ChooseTest3.fss:125 left unedited. It carries the same out-of-range numeral as IntegerChoose2.fss:114 but is named in no .test file and LibraryJUTest.java:36 sweeps .test files only, so no gate covers it and no measurement of a repair would be available. Recorded as a new ledger row rather than edited unverified.

The ladder driver not run. explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv shows every file of the ladder corpus holding a numeral of bit length 32 or 64 — NumeralTest, NumberPrintTest, formatTest, sequivTest, BitTwiddle, UnsignedTest, BigNum, simpleExp, realArith — with compile return code 255 and an empty run column, failing in one or two seconds before code generation, so no ladder row can move either way. toolu_01LL4pwhB1a2o2Eb92qU7WPX.summary:
The branch was relaunched after the container died: commit 7e666704 held the failing test and probes/junit-before.out, and the worktree held uncommitted edits whose last log line showed Integer.test starting and never finishing. Everything was re-run rather than trusted, including javap on the built classes, and the measurements phase B never reached were taken fresh.

Part one is the repair the brief describes. CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr's bounds become bitLength() <= 31 and <= 63, exact for both signs; FIntLiteral.asNN64 learns to read the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps, which was forced and measured (junit-codegen-only.out); asNN32's range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything, is made to mean what it says, which was a decision and not forced — the brief's premise about asNN32 is corrected in the report.

Part one then turned library_tests/Integer.test from green to four failures, all one thing: a radix numeral whose value is outside the annotated signed type, written to mean a two's-complement bit pattern. literals.tex:104-108 gives such a numeral the value of its digits in its radix, and probes r2g and r2h show the interpreter has always refused the idiom, so these are not correct programs the repair broke — they are programs the language does not accept, on which the two paths now agree. The repair reduces divergence and creates none.

The blast radius was enumerated by value in every radix rather than grepped decimally, which is how the radix-16 half was found. Eighteen lines on the compile path, twelve in range and now right for the right reason, six out of range. Five are repaired: ZZ32_MIN and ZZ64_MIN in the prelude (value-identical, in FortressLibrary.fss:703's spelling), twiceHuge in Integer3 and Integer4 (value-identical, same bit pattern written legally, assertions unchanged), and IntegerChoose2, where 3037000500 is bound at ZZ64 so the test exercises the fast/slow boundary its comment names instead of a negative i. Integer.test is OK (27 tests) again; the rung's own test passes.

The batch's one named stop was tested and is not met: the branch in forIntLiteralExpr chooses an overload of FIntLiteral.make, never a type, every numeral still has the flat static type Types.INT_LITERAL, and r2e and p39 show the arithmetic still happening at IntLiteral — it merely starts from the right operand now. That fork is untouched and still open. Three new ledger rows are owed and named in record.md.
